title: HTML Quiz
description: Thirteen questions covering the whole HTML tutorial: document structure, elements and attributes, text, links, images, tables, forms, semantics and SEO.

questions.question: What must be the first line of an HTML document?
questions.explanation: `<!DOCTYPE html>` tells the browser to use standards mode. It comes before the `<html>` element.

questions.question: The global attribute that must be unique on a page and is used by fragment links such as `#pricing` is `___`.
questions.explanation: `id` identifies a single element; `class` may be shared by many.

questions.question: How many `<h1>` elements should a typical page contain?
questions.explanation: One `<h1>` describing the page's main subject keeps the outline clear for users and search engines.

questions.question: From the page `/docs/guide/intro.html`, where does `href="/images/logo.png"` point?
questions.explanation: A leading slash makes the path relative to the site root, regardless of the current folder.

questions.question: What accessibility problem does this image have?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute is missing entirely, so screen readers announce the file name. Add descriptive alt text (or alt="" if decorative).
options: It is missing an alt attribute
Width and height are not allowed together
PNG images need a type attribute

questions.question: Which attribute makes a cell span three columns?
Which attribute makes an ordered list count down from its last number?
questions.explanation: The boolean `reversed` attribute numbers the items in descending order.

questions.question: An input without a `name` attribute is still included when the form is submitted.
questions.explanation: Only fields with a name are submitted. A field without one is silently left out.

questions.question: Which input type shows a numeric keypad on phones and validates the format of the value?
questions.explanation: `type="email"` shows an email keyboard and validates the format. `tel` shows a number pad but does not validate; `text` does neither.

questions.question: Which element lets screen-reader users jump directly to the primary content of a page?
questions.explanation: `<main>` is exposed as the main landmark; users can jump to it with one keystroke.

questions.question: Which tag tells search engines the preferred URL when the same content is reachable at several addresses?
questions.explanation: `<link rel="canonical">` names the preferred URL so ranking signals are not split between duplicates.
